full_judgment: 2. The facts led to the case, in short, are that the respondent No.1 as pre-emptor instituted Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No.54 of 2000 in the 4th Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Narayangonj for pre-emption under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 alleging, inter-alia, that the land covering an area of .56 acres of Plot No.1 and 0.24 acre of Plot No.2 of Jangalia mouza originally belonged to Rahimuddin, Tamizudding and Naimuddin. The land covering an area of 0.38 acre of Plot No.3 and 0.44 acre of Plot No.5 originally belonged to said Naimuddin, Tamizudding and Rahimuddin. They purchased the said land on the basis of the registered kabala deed dated 21.03.1950. Rahimuddin purchased the said land in the benami of his son Zamir Ali. While owning and possessing the land of the aforesaid plots namely, Plot Nos.l, 2, 3 and 5 Rahimuddin died leaving behind Zamir Ali, Akber Ali, Zinnat Ali, Niat Ali @ Niaz Ali and Ambor Ali as 5 sons and Sewar Bibi and Khaitun Bibi as two daughters. Ambor Ali died leaving behind 3 sons Misir Ali, Mohammad Ali and Abdul Mannan, pre-emptor petitioner and one daughter Anwara, opposite party No.23 and a widow Tafiran Nessa, opposite party No.24 in S.A. and R.S. record of right were prepared in the name of Tamizuddin, Naimuddin, Zamir Ali, Akbor Ali, Zinnat Ali, Niat Ali @ Newaz Ali, Misir Ali, Mohammad Ali and pre-emptor Abdul Mannan. As the daughters of Rahimuddin and Ambor Ali were living with their respective husbands in different Faziul Karim,,I)273 places, so their names were not recorded inadvertently in S.A. and R.S. Khatian, Naimuddin while owning and possessing his share executed a Heba-bil-Ewaz deed for 0.44 acre of land of Plot No.5 dated 18.06.1974 in favour of Misir Ali, Mohammad Ali and pre-emptor petitioner Abdul Mannan delivered possession. Tamizudding died leaving behind one son, Vendor opposite party No.2 Nabir Hossain, one daughter opposite party No.3 Sabitum as his heir. Satunnessa while owning and possessing 0.24 acre of land by way of inheritance and purchase from Plot Nos.l, 2 and 3 and some other lands of the undisputed Plot No.993, sold the same to Misir Ali, Mohammad Ali and pre-emptor Abdul Mannan by kabala deed dated 05.07.1979. The pre-emptor acquiring the title and possession by way of inheritance, by Heba-bil-Ewaz deed and by way of purchase and thus becoming co-sharer of the land under pre-emption he has been possessing his share along with other co-sharers of the disputed jama. There was no metes and bound partition among the co-sharers of the jama. The vendor opposite party No.2 Nabir Hossain without informing of the co-sharers or without issuing statutory notice to the co-sharers transferred the land under pre-emption to the opposite party No.1 Abdul Awal Ratan by the kabala deed dated 29.08.2000. The pre-emptor came to know about the disputed deed on 31.08.2000 from the pre-emptor opposite party No. 1. Accordingly, he made search to the Arai-Hazar, Sub-registrar office and obtained the certified copy of the disputed deed on 03.09.2000 and found that the instant transfer was done at a consideration of Tk.60,000.00. The pre-emptor opposite party No.1 Abdul Awal Ratan is a stranger purchaser. The pre-emptee petitioner has got necessity of the disputed land and he has got less than 20 bighas of land and as such, he is entitled to get the disputed land by way of pre-emption. So, depositing the consideration and compensation money he instituted the instant application for pre-emption.
